text:
Minnesota scored three times in the first 17 minutes and spent the rest of the night making sure Vegas never got close enough to matter. The Wild had the better of the chances all game, 4.27 expected goals to 2.75, and the simulated replays give them the win 62 percent of the time. The one lopsided period was the second, when MIN out-chanced VGK 1.40 to 0.37.

The early burst did the damage. Matt Boldy opened the scoring at 11:50 off assists from Olli Maatta and Quinn Hughes, and Maxim Shabanov converted the game's only power play at 14:32 on what the model rated a 4 percent chance. Danila Yurov made it 3-0 at 16:57. Vegas went 0 for 5 with the man advantage, and Minnesota took 15 penalty minutes to VGK's 7, so the Golden Knights had every opportunity to claw back and could not.

Rasmus Andersson scored on a 3 percent slap shot early in the second, and William Karlsson cut it to 2-3 in the third, which gave Vegas a pulse. Minnesota answered at 18:38 when Joel Eriksson Ek scored on a 52 percent look, set up by Kirill Kaprizov. Eriksson Ek's line was on the ice for 2.72 expected goals for against 0.79 against. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 21 of 23 shots, 0.75 goals better than expected, and Carter Hart stopped 24 of 27 for VGK.
